ratings_why.fun: Keep-or-swap, which texts to borrow and where to sit Turncoat and the Lady give a real puzzle every turn; the only drag is reading boards of stacked texts.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because a Guise carries its tribe, so a Changeling becomes a Bird that flies south or an Ooze with a Belly, and Exchange turns the shop into storage. No tribe today plays across other tribes' keywords or trades with the shop.

verdict_why: The v3 rewrites of Placement Officer and the Fetch tied Exchange and Guise together; what's left is rules wording and playtest edges, not a design fix.

points.text: The tribe crossing is the gem: a Cradle Kit in a Bird's Guise flies south and comes home doubled, still in its Guise. Show one cross-tribe example per lobby tribe in the folio so players find these.

Placement Officer with Coat-Peg Steward moves both a Guise and its stats onto a fresh shop unit, so you can upgrade a body each turn. Pair it with Wicker Moll and the old text stays behind on a Stock too: one swap, three gains.
The Lady picks up a fight Guise from Turncoat Hare or Penny Second only if she sits after them in reading order, which makes slot order a puzzle. Say so in her reminder text so the puzzle is visible.
Pip Unlike mirroring a Hedgerow Pass into a leftmost lane is the best off-label use here. One more Changeling card that reads directional text (beside, in front of) would widen it.
Midnight Swap on a 0-value Stock is a 2-gold unit for any tribe, so Changelings give the whole lobby a shop trick. Good cross-player texture; keep an eye on its price.

standouts.why: Turns shop units into Changelings, so Exchange and Guise now feed each other.
Belly, Mire and Pass on one body: the payoff for drafting a two-tribe board.
Mirror-backwards copies make directional text from other tribes do new things.

weakest.why: A plain End of Turn buffer; it adds no decision beyond wearing any Guise.
Just counts Exchanges and pays stats; the Exchange line deserves a payoff that plays with the shop.
Overlaps the Cradle Kit and asks you to sell good units to get good text.

flags.note: Not clear whether Grandfer Acorn pays when Placement Officer moves a Guise or Wicker Moll's Stock arrives wearing one.
Keeper of the Lost Hour with the Lady doubles every fight Guise she holds; the high roll is meant, but worth the owner's eye.
Midnight Swap plus a free Stock gives any tribe a 2-gold unit.
